episodes.164012: A robust cold front swept through the Rio Grande Valley/Deep South Texas region and the Lower Texas coastal waters late in the afternoon of December 18th. A line of broken showers and thunderstorms developed along the cold front as it headed southeast through the region. Some of the thunderstorms produced strong winds that were recorded at some of the buoys and Texas Coastal Oceanic Observation Network (TCOON) sites as they moved through.
episodes.165305: Southerly winds ahead of a cold front brought high moisture levels into South Florida, leading to heavy showers and thunderstorms over eastern sections of Palm Beach County.
episodes.165358: Showers and thunderstorms over the Lower and Middle Florida Keys were in advance of an approaching cold front, passing through the central Gulf of Mexico.  Isolated gale-force wind gusts were occurring along the reef offshore Marathon.
episodes.165389: A cold front moving across southeast Louisiana was the focus for a line of showers and thunderstorms. One of these thunderstorms managed to strengthen just enough to produce gale force wind gusts over portions of Lake Pontchartrain.

events.county: Laguna Madre From Port Of Brownsville To Arroyo Colorado
events.narrative: A strong thunderstorm associated with a cold front developed between Port Mansfield and the Laguna Atascosa Wildlife Refuge late in the afternoon on December 18th. The Realitos Peninsula TCOON site recorded gusts of 34 knots between 6:54 PM CST and 7:18 PM CST.
The Weatherflow mesonet at Mid Lake Pontchartrain measured a 41 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
The Lakefront Airport ASOS measured a 47 mph thunderstorm wind gust.

events.county: Hawk Channel From Craig Key To West End Of Seven Mile Bridge Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A southerly wind gust of 40 knots was measured at the new Sombrero Key Light.

Heavy rainfall shortly before sunrise on December 19th led to flooding of streets in downtown Lake Worth Beach. Main areas affected were along the Lucerne and Lake Avenue corridor, east of I-95 to near Lake Worth Golf Club. Water entered the first floor units of an apartment complex at North F Street, caused by poor drainage in the immediate vicinity. ||A nearby rain gauge measured a total of 4.93 inches of rain between 3:14 AM and 6:49 AM, with over 4 inches falling in just 2 hours. Rainfall estimates from South Florida Water Management District were in the 4-6 inch range in the affected area.
